For more flexible program production, the automatic generation of new speaking styles and descriptions from past programs and multimodal support are topics for further study. We are working on applying our DNN-TTS system to a variety of applications. For example, we created automated audio descriptions for the visually impaired.3 We plan to use an automatic news reader that uses our system for local radio.29 When it is a challenge to arrange an anchor for emergency news at off-peak hours, it may be possible to solve such problems with our system. For the visually impaired, a service that automatically reads aloud captions of breaking news is needed. Moreover, by developing a controllable TTS system, these in conjunction with more new services using TTS deserve further study. Conclusion We described various applications for our DNN-TTS system with regard to automated services and a TV-studio program for AI news anchor and we experimentally demonstrated that synthesized speech with a slow rate is much better than standard-speed speech synthesis for language learners. We also found that our system contributes not only to production automation, but also universal services. Our system can not only replace existing broadcasting services, but also generate new services. Speech synthesis is a promising technology for broadcasting services but there is room for improvement. TTS has made it possible to automate many broadcasting services, for example, providing the latest news through synthesized speech. The benefits of operating TTS for broadcasters are not only directly related to their services, but also the ease of acquiring training data for deep learning-based TTS. Collecting data for TTS is very expensive, but archives of TV programs can easily be used for training data. We hope that broadcasters will use TTS for their programs to create interesting content and improve business efficiency.
